movements.name: Back Squat
movements.summary: The Back Squat is a foundational movement within the Squat Pattern. It develops coordinated joint motion, muscular control, and load tolerance. This movement supports performance, injury resilience, and long-term movement quality.
muscles: Primary movers responsible for force production
cues: Establish trunk control before initiating movement
Move through the full available range with control
Maintain symmetry and balanced load distribution
Control the eccentric phase before accelerating
faults: Loss of trunk stability leading to compensation
Asymmetric loading due to dominant-side bias
Restricted range caused by mobility limitations
Speed prioritized over control
injury_notes: If pain occurs, regress range and load and prioritize control.
Avoid positions that provoke sharp pain; use an alternative pattern.
coaching: Set your stance and brace before movement
Move through the full controlled range
Maintain symmetry and balance
Finish strong without rushing the end position
movements.description: Perform the Back Squat by setting the bar securely across your upper back, bracing your core, and maintaining a neutral spine. Initiate the movement by hinging at the hips and bending the knees simultaneously, keeping your chest tall and knees tracking over the toes. Descend until the hips reach at least parallel depth while maintaining balance through the mid-foot. Drive upward through the heels, extending hips and knees together while keeping the torso stable and controlled. Maintain steady breathing, consistent tempo, and full-body tension throughout the movement.
tips: Do not let knees collapse inward

Lower until you feel stretch in hamstrings
Drive hips forward to return to standing
